# #183 A1 independent second review: BLOCK

Head: `1fbe9476be242214d143e65bd7e011fc1ea545b5`

Whole capability-model review, using merge-base `d7389056ab7f8e0eaf309d1db1229c760337ba5d`. The supplied main `a244cb4` is newer; a two-way tree diff would incorrectly attribute later main changes/removals to this PR. No verdict is assigned to cancelled `a08c2648` or skipped `c940386`.

The worktree remains clean and pinned, but GitHub has become **DIRTY** as main advanced. The green CI below predates that conflict and is not current-base merge proof. The source findings require repair independently of reconciliation.

## Findings

**F001, medium: non-Copilot ownership is assigned to a short-lived connector.**

`http/mod.rs:1107-1162,1230-1271` sets `CapabilityIssue.owner` from the accepted socket peer for every harness; `core/capability.rs:391-410` persists it unchanged. A CLI child below a live OMP/Pi/Claude/Codex harness becomes the recorded owner. Once that child exits, `registration.rs:1699-1705` treats the capability's live holder as gone although the harness remains alive.

AC4 requires those owners to be the verified harness process, not the connecting child. Keep the real peer evidence separate from the ownership assignment; bind non-Copilot ownership to the verified harness boundary. Test a child bootstrap followed by child exit, with the harness still live and a proofless move still refused. PM confirmed this requirement in `0c6b0d44985b4f88-0000000000000003`.

**F002, medium: ordinary cancellation releases state that an owned commit still needs.**

`registration.rs:1258` keeps the boundary admission only in the awaiting registration future. Native registration is shielded by `reports.exclusively`, but ordinary registration uses `work.await` (`http/mod.rs:1336-1354`). EventBus independently owns admitted registry work through commit/publication (`events/mod.rs:155-185`).

Dropping an ordinary waiter after that admission releases its capacity reservation and registration mutex before the write finishes. Another boundary can reserve the same last slot. Cancellation also skips the capability resync at `registration.rs:1469`. On a peer reissue at the same boundary, the put observer does not forget the old digest merely because ownership/digest changed; an old token can remain in the warm map although the store now holds only its replacement.

Keep admission, serialization and post-commit capability resync with the independently owned registration lifetime, not just the caller. The controlled regression must pause an admitted commit, abort the waiter, refuse another boundary until completion, and prove the first row actually commits; include the same-boundary old-token-invalid check. This independently observed issue also corresponds to **P183-F002**, as PM confirmed.

The successful nonce counter is likewise incremented only in the outer HTTP success branch (`mod.rs:1385`). A cancelled waiter can commit a nonce-authenticated issuance without recording that success. Move committed-success accounting into the owned completion path.

**F003, medium: a stale proven-close label can exempt the wrong capability from the reissue mark.**

Auth retains `TokenEvidence::Live(SeatId)`, not a generation/digest, before handler/body work (`mod.rs:818-850`). Close later derives its proven suffix from that cached value (`lifecycle.rs:363-364`), including across a held memory turn. The revoking transaction trusts the suffix when deciding whether to write a reissue mark (`store/capability.rs:315-346`).

A T1-authenticated close can be delayed while T2 is rotated and presented, retiring T1. The delayed close can still revoke T2 as proven and leave no mark. The descriptor CAS does not verify which capability justified the exemption.

Carry the presented digest to the revoking write and check it against the capability being revoked. A stale proof remains an allowed public-facts close, but is **unproven**: it still revokes and sets the mark. Test the delayed T1/T2 sequence and subsequent nonce-required bootstrap. PM explicitly required this in `0c6b0d44985b4f88-000000000000000e`.

**F004, medium: composite role/prime operations are missing from the counters and inventory.**

Registration declares/counts only `registration`, then a non-resume `claim.role` calls `roles.assert_role` (`registration.rs:1526-1527`). Project create/set with `--prime` updates the designated prime (`governance.rs:714-727,753-778`), while `governance_class` and `/v1/project` inventory declare only attribution.

Count and inventory every class actually exercised: role-and-holder in addition to registration/attribution on these branches. Preserve ordinary no-role/no-prime and read-only controls. When counting inside owned work, retain the request evidence rather than losing its task-local proof. PM confirmed the composite rule in `0c6b0d44985b4f88-0000000000000011`.

**F005, medium: a walk can combine different PID generations into one authorized hop.**

`http/provenance.rs:207-231` reads a process start and then its parent/name separately. If the PID exits/recycles between those reads, the accepted old start can be combined with the replacement's parent. A peer originally outside H can appear below registered H; H's older start satisfies the child-start comparison, so that comparison does not detect this mixture.

Use a coherent per-hop process tuple or recheck the start after reading parent/name, before matching/following it. Add an injected-reader case where the first start matches the accepted peer, parent/name comes from a reused PID under H, and the next start differs. This is source-confirmed permitted ordering, not a live exploitation claim. No new regression receipt was available for this case.

## What was verified

The nonce consume, seat/capability write and predecessor retirement are one owned registry transaction, with proof/reissue-mark rechecks before mutation. Refused issuance preserves predecessors; expiry cleanup affects the expired nonce only. Ordinary nonce replay remains refused and audited.

Rotation presentations share the store-first retirement path; the warm-map retirement is conditional on the confirmed generation. Store retirement failure propagates. Tombstone, process-changing registry writes and reconcile revoke digests transactionally; unproven revocations mark the seat, and peer issuance checks that mark again inside the write.

The socket is private, uses accepted-stream credentials, and the walk is bounded with no ancestry cache. Roots precede target/index matching. Hosted lookup visits at most two entries. The remote listener checks the header, activity token and registration nonce carriers before their effects. The spawn nonce is file-handed at 0600, not placed in argv; the wrapper consumes it into the harness environment. Empty exit status is now not-yet-exited, and the writer stages/renames its status.

These conclusions do not close the five findings or enforce any ordinary effect class. **A1 must not merge/deploy alone; A2 stacks and deploys with it.** Send-as and the other effect gates remain outside A1.

## Proof and cost ceiling

[CI 42499154071](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42499154071), associated with this exact head, attempt 1: **2316 Rust cases passed; six skipped**. Artifact `13624429724`, JUnit timestamp `2026-11-08T16:20:01.356+00:00`, contains no failures/errors. Existing issuer, owner-live, reissue, rotation, root, cap-race, contract, directory-read counting and empty-status cases executed. Both Node checks, Rust lint and Delivers passed. `git diff --check` passed.

Author `a1r2-mut/INDEX.md` records 18 kills, largely on working trees that became `ea1dedb` and `a08c2648`; EMPTY ran on the tree that became this head. Batches 1/2 were multi-mutant and attributed by assertion. D9 mutated memory only. The index documents inherited-site/assertion checks, not 18 isolated exact-head reruns. The new findings' regressions have been requested through PM; no such executed proof is claimed here.

The new Unix listener loop is event-driven per connection, with a one-second backoff only on accept faults. Token checks add a hash/map compare; tokenless checks add a bounded in-process walk. Boot rebuild/nonce expiry is one-time; no nonce sweep. D5 adds a pane read once per spawn. No new per-seat polling/process launch was established; admission soundness remains blocked by F002, and live cost readings remain owed at joint A1/A2 deploy.

No local builds/tests, exploit, credential-file reads, dependency installs, product edits or canonical plan-state edits were performed. Fix the findings, reconcile main and request a new final-head review.
